title: Monster Spawner
hints: A vector that grows moves or copies its monsters into new memory, and the old ones are destroyed, so you may see more "destroyed" messages than you expect. Call `reserve` first and the extra messages disappear: that is a good thing to explain in a comment.
For `createRandom`, keep a `static const std::array` of name, type and HP rows inside the function and return a `Monster` built from a random row.
requirements: `class Monster` with `enum class Type` nested, name, HP, damage
Static live-count and total-created counters; IDs from a static
`static Monster createRandom()` factory using a static random table (`std::array` of templates)
Spawn monsters in scopes and vectors — predict the order of destruction messages
